title: Memorized arrangements, singing and the band's light style
summary: The band memorized its own numbers, he sang West Indies Blues, and the group's style came from one trumpet and one trombone.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I heard you take a break back there on the banjo.
A little break. How much reading did you all do on a tune like that?

Well uh, we, we part of it was a bunch of gifted musicians. We practically memorized all those numbers. See? You know that that is the sport. We played them so many times. See? And we just memorized them. In fact we played a whole, a waterfall show without any music. All our own numbers. West Indies Blues was uh, a number thawed up by Pierron and uh, I don't know who else had anything to do with it. I sang it all the way through. In fact I was entertaining the band at all times. That's Mama's Gone Goodbye. Pete wrote that too. Him and Pierron I think.
I think he told me he wrote the music and Pierron wrote the words.
Yeah. Well Pierron was more of a lyric writer you see. Now Purple Rose I think it was, I'm not positive but I think it was more Pierron than Steele.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Were these the tunes that you played on the job? Yeah.
Did you... That was our style. Yeah. Right there. Yeah.
That was our style, yeah, right there. We had a light band because we only had one trumpet and one trompon. Like now you have a low-ish brass section.
